t: Minimum Lights to Illuminate a Road — Greedy Jump Covering
o: 'Understanding the problem': Some positions have bulbs with given radii; we may add radius-1 bulbs anywhere, and we want full coverage of [0, n−1] with fewest added bulbs. In example 1 there are no bulbs, so bulbs at 1 and 3 (covering [0,2] and [2,3]) suffice — 2 bulbs. In example 2 the bulb at index 3 with v=2 covers [1,4], leaving only position 0 dark; one added bulb fixes it. With n up to 10⁵ we need a linear-ish greedy, not exponential placement search.
k: Treat every bulb (existing or added) as an interval; this is minimum interval cover where existing intervals are free.
If position p is uncovered, placing an added bulb at p+1 covers p..p+2, so we can jump 3 ahead — greedy jumps give optimality.
Precompute far[p] = the largest right endpoint among existing bulbs covering p, via sorting bulbs by left endpoint and sweeping a running maximum.

a.i: Scan left to right maintaining the first possibly-dark position pos. If an existing bulb covers pos and reaches far[pos], everything up to far[pos] is lit by that single contiguous interval, so jump past it for free. Otherwise pos is dark; the best single added bulb covers at most 3 consecutive positions, so put it at pos+1 and jump to pos+3. This exchange argument (each added bulb covers ≤3 new positions, and we never skip a free extension) proves minimality.
s: Collect existing bulbs as (left,right) intervals, sort by left, and sweep positions computing far[p] = max right among bulbs with left ≤ p.
Set pos = 0, ans = 0; while pos < n: if far[pos] ≥ pos, set pos = far[pos]+1; else increment ans and set pos = pos+3.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting the bulb intervals dominates; the sweeps are linear.
a.sp: O(n) — the far array and interval list.

a.i: Model added bulbs as candidate intervals [j−1, j+1] for every j, merge them conceptually with free intervals, and run the classic 'pick the interval covering the current gap that extends furthest right' greedy using a max-heap of active right endpoints. It yields the same result but demonstrates the general interval-cover template.
s: Push all bulb intervals sorted by left endpoint; sweep the gap start g from 0.
Pop all intervals with left ≤ g into a max-heap of right endpoints; if the heap's best right < g, place an added bulb covering [g, g+2] (count it, treat as interval) and continue.
Advance g to bestRight+1; repeat until g ≥ n.
a.t: O(n log n) — each interval is pushed/popped once from the heap.

w: Wrap-up: Prefer Approach 1 in interviews — it is simpler and strictly faster in practice. Common pitfalls: forgetting to clamp bulb ranges to [0, n−1], assuming coverage from far[pos] extends contiguously (justify via the single-interval argument), and off-by-one on the +3 jump (a radius-1 bulb covers exactly 3 positions). Follow-ups: what if added bulbs had radius r (jump 2r+1), or bulbs could be removed for profit?
